key_insight: Shared Gaussianization (SG) is a Gaussian regularizer that certifies both alignment and uniformity in contrastive learning, matching InfoNCE’s optimum while revealing when the objectives still differ away from that optimum.
engineering_relevance: For self-supervised representation learning, SG provides a computable loss with theoretical guarantees on InfoNCE excess, plus a principled way to tune alignment versus style-nuisance removal.
method: Tests Gaussianity of the averaged pair of normalized views using a characteristic-function criterion with an independent chi-radius.
Connects SG loss to population InfoNCE excess via a sharp square-root bound and dimension-free constants.
Analyzes when kernel spectra and alignment weights eliminate nuisance retention; uses an off-diagonal U-statistic to reduce finite-batch bias.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports controlled latent-variable experiments and LeJEPA batch-size studies showing measured gains separate style-retaining from style-free encoders, and that InfoNCE can achieve lower SG loss than SG-trained models from scratch.
watch_item: The guarantees are population-level and the finite-batch estimator can be biased, so performance depends on kernel choice, alignment weight, and batch size.
paper_title: Shared Gaussianization: What Gaussian Regularizers Certify About Contrastive Learning, and What They Miss
